source.text: שִׁ֗יר הַֽמַּ֫עֲל֥וֹתאֶל־יְ֭הוָה בַּצָּרָ֣תָה לִּ֑י קָ֝רָ֗אתִי וַֽיַּעֲנֵֽנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: The song of the ascents. To YHWH in the distress to me I called, and he answered me.

en.L: A song of ascents. To {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in my distress I called, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered me.
en.B: A song of ascents. When I was in trouble I cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave me an answer.
en.R: A song for the journey up to Jerusalem. When I was in trouble, I called to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered me.

fr.L: Cantique des montées. Vers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, dans ma détresse, j’ai crié, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a répondu.
fr.B: Cantique des montées. Quand j’étais dans la détresse, j’ai crié vers {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a donné une réponse.
fr.R: Chant pour la montée vers Jérusalem. Quand j’étais en difficulté, j’ai appelé {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}. Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} m’a répondu.

sw.L: Wimbo wa kupanda. Kwa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} katika dhiki yangu nililia, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akanijibu.
sw.B: Wimbo wa kupanda. Nilipokuwa katika taabu nilimlilia {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} akanijibu.
sw.R: Wimbo wa safari ya kupanda kwenda Yerusalemu. Nilipokuwa na shida, nilimwita {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. Naye akanijibu.

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: This psalm's title is short and the Hebrew counts it together with the first line as verse 1, so here the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number. This is so in all fifteen Songs of Ascents (Psalms 120-134).

decisions.choice: a song of ascents: probably a pilgrim song
alternatives: a song for the temple steps
a song in rising steps of verse
a song of the return from exile
decisions.reason: Each of the fifteen psalms 120-134 carries this title. "Ascents" (ma'alot) means goings up. They were probably sung by pilgrims going up to Jerusalem for the festivals, as 122:1-4 describes (Exodus 23:17; Deuteronomy 16:16). The same word is used of the return from exile in Ezra 7:9, and of steps; other explanations have therefore been given, and the exact sense is not certain.

decisions.choice: past tense: he answered me before
alternatives: present: I call and he answers
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the form usually used for past events. The psalmist remembers that the LORD answered in an earlier trouble, and on that ground prays again in verse 2. Some read the verbs as describing what always happens ("I call, and he answers").

decisions.choice: A song for the journey up to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Readable says what the title most likely means (see the meaning decision on "ascents"); Literal and Balanced keep the title as it stands.

decisions.choice: "Cantique des montées" (Literal, Balanced); "Chant pour la montée vers Jérusalem" (Readable), for the title of Psalms 120-134
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the song of the ascents". Literal and Balanced keep its words, as the terms note sets for the fifteen Songs of Ascents; Readable says what the title probably means, a song for pilgrims going up to Jerusalem, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "le SEIGNEUR" for the divine name, with "Yahvé" under the reader setting; the speaker prays with "tu"
decisions.reason: The French default writes the name as "le SEIGNEUR" in capitals, like the English "the LORD"; "l'Éternel", the Segond tradition, is the form a reviewer may prefer. In these psalms the speaker addresses God with "tu", the ordinary French of prayer.

decisions.choice: "Wimbo wa kupanda" (L, B); "Wimbo wa safari ya kupanda kwenda Yerusalemu" (R), in every title of Psalms 120-134
decisions.reason: The title says only "a song of the ascents". Literal and Balanced keep that word, "kupanda" (going up); Readable says where the pilgrims went up to, as the English Readable does, since these were probably songs for the road up to Jerusalem (see the meaning decision).

decisions.choice: BWANA in capitals, with Yahwe as the alternative; free pronouns for God such as "naye" carry the deity_pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As in the rest of the Swahili Old Testament. Swahili marks most pronouns inside the verb ("akanijibu", he answered me), where a capital is impossible, so only free pronouns and possessives for God carry the setting.

source.text: יְֽהוָ֗ה הַצִּ֣ילָה נַ֭פְשִׁי מִשְּׂפַת־שֶׁ֑קֶר מִלָּשׁ֥וֹן רְמִיָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: YHWH, deliver my soul from a lip of falsehood, from a tongue of deceit.

en.L: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, deliver my soul from a lip of falsehood, from a tongue of deceit.
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, rescue me from people whose lips tell lies, whose tongues deceive.
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, save me from liars and from people who trick others.

fr.L: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, délivre mon âme de la lèvre de mensonge, de la langue de tromperie.
fr.B: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, arrache-moi aux gens dont les lèvres mentent, dont la langue trompe.
fr.R: {{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, sauve-moi des menteurs et des gens qui trompent les autres.

sw.L: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, uiokoe nafsi yangu na mdomo wa uongo, na ulimi wa hila.
sw.B: Ee {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, uniokoe na watu ambao midomo yao husema uongo, ambao ndimi zao hudanganya.
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, niokoe kutoka kwa waongo na kwa watu wanaowadanganya wengine.

decisions.choice: lip, tongue: the people who speak
decisions.reason: "A lip of falsehood" and "a tongue of deceit" stand for the people who speak that way. The psalm does not say what the lies were; verses 6-7 set them against the psalmist's wish for peace.

decisions.choice: deceit: treachery
decisions.reason: The word (remiyyah) means deceit or treachery, words meant to mislead (52:6; Micah 6:12).

decisions.choice: my soul (L); me (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Psalms 1-12, nefesh is "soul" at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "me" or "my life", since the word means the whole living person.

decisions.choice: people whose lips tell lies (B); liars (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the people that the lips and tongue stand for (m1).

decisions.choice: "mon âme" at Literal; "moi" at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: Nefesh is "âme" at Literal, as the terms note sets; here it stands for the whole person, so Balanced and Readable say "me", as the English does.

decisions.choice: "nafsi yangu" (my soul) at Literal; "mimi" (me) at Balanced and Readable, through Psalms 120-150
decisions.reason: The Hebrew nefesh is the whole living person. Literal keeps the word "nafsi"; Balanced and Readable say the person, as the English does. "Roho" would suggest the spirit apart from the body.

source.text: מַה־יִּתֵּ֣ן לְ֭ךָ וּמַה־יֹּסִ֥יף לָ֗ךְ לָשׁ֥וֹן רְמִיָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: What will he give to you, and what will he add to you, tongue of deceit?

en.L: What will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} give to you, and what will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} add to you, [you] tongue of deceit?
en.B: You deceitful tongue, what will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} give you, and what more will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} heap on you?
en.R: You liars, what will God give you in return? What more will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} add?

fr.L: Que te donnera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}, et que t’ajoutera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}, langue de tromperie ?
fr.B: Langue trompeuse, que te donnera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}}, et que fera-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} pleuvoir encore sur toi ?
fr.R: Menteurs, que va-t-il vous arriver de la part de Dieu ? Que va-t-{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} encore ajouter ?

sw.L: Atakupa nini, na atakuongezea nini, [wewe] ulimi wa hila?
sw.B: Ewe ulimi wa udanganyifu, atakupa nini, na atakuzidishia nini zaidi?
sw.R: Ninyi waongo, Mungu atawapa nini kama malipo? Ataongeza nini zaidi?

decisions.choice: give ... add: the words of an oath of punishment
decisions.reason: "May God do so to you and add more" was a way of calling down punishment (1 Samuel 3:17; Ruth 1:17). The question takes up those words: what will God do to the liar, and what more besides? Verse 4 gives the answer.

decisions.choice: he: God
alternatives: impersonal: what shall be given to you
decisions.reason: The verbs have "he" as subject. In the oath formula that "he" is God, so the liar is asked what God will give in return. The verbs may also be impersonal, "what shall be done to you".

decisions.choice: tongue of deceit: spoken to the liar
decisions.reason: The psalmist turns and speaks directly to the "deceitful tongue" of verse 2, that is, to the liar.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who gives (m2), and speaks to "liars" (m3).

decisions.choice: "Menteurs" with "vous" at Readable, where Literal and Balanced speak to the "langue" with "tu"
decisions.reason: The tongue stands for the liars, as the English Readable says "You liars"; French then needs the plural "vous".

source.text: חִצֵּ֣י גִבּ֣וֹר שְׁנוּנִ֑ים עִ֝֗ם גַּחֲלֵ֥י רְתָמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Arrows of a warrior, sharpened, with coals of broom plants.

en.L: Arrows of a warrior, sharpened, with coals of broom [wood]!
en.B: Sharpened arrows from a fighter's bow, and hot coals of broom wood!
en.R: Here is what you will get: a soldier's sharp arrows and red-hot coals that burn a long time.

fr.L: Des flèches de guerrier, aiguisées, avec des braises de genêt !
fr.B: Les flèches aiguisées d’un combattant, et des braises ardentes de genêt !
fr.R: Voici ce que vous recevrez : les flèches pointues d’un soldat et des braises brûlantes qui restent chaudes longtemps.

sw.L: Mishale ya shujaa, iliyonolewa, pamoja na makaa ya [mti wa] mretemu!
sw.B: Mishale mikali ya mpiganaji hodari, na makaa ya moto ya mti wa mretemu!
sw.R: Hiki ndicho mtakachopata: mishale mikali ya askari, na makaa ya moto yanayowaka kwa muda mrefu.

decisions.choice: the answer to verse 3: the punishment
alternatives: a picture of the deceitful tongue itself
decisions.reason: The verse answers the question of verse 3: the liar will receive sharp arrows and burning coals, a fitting reward for a tongue that wounds like arrows and burns like fire (57:5; 64:4; James 3:6). Others read it as a description of the tongue itself.

decisions.choice: broom: a desert shrub that burns hot and long
decisions.reason: The broom (rotem) is a shrub of the desert (1 Kings 19:4; Job 30:4). Its wood makes charcoal that burns very hot and keeps its heat a long time.

decisions.choice: Here is what you will get
decisions.reason: Readable makes the link to the question of verse 3 explicit (m1), and says what broom coals are like (m2).

decisions.choice: "genêt" for the broom shrub
decisions.reason: The rotem is the white broom of the desert, "genêt" in French; its charcoal burns hot and long, which Readable explains instead of naming the plant.

decisions.choice: "mretemu" for the broom bush
decisions.reason: "Mretemu" is the Swahili name of the broom bush of the desert, whose wood makes hot, long-lasting coals; Readable says what the coals do instead of naming the plant, as the English Readable does.

source.text: אֽוֹיָה־לִ֭י כִּי־גַ֣רְתִּי מֶ֑שֶׁךְ שָׁ֝כַ֗נְתִּי עִֽם־אָהֳלֵ֥י קֵדָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Woe to me, that I have sojourned [in] Meshech, I have dwelt with [the] tents of Kedar.

en.L: Woe to me, that I sojourn [in] Meshech, [that] I dwell among [the] tents of Kedar!
en.B: How miserable I am, living as a foreigner in Meshech, making my home among the tents of Kedar!
en.R: How terrible it is for me! I am like a stranger living far away in Meshech, or among the tents of Kedar.

fr.L: Malheur à moi, car je séjourne [à] Méshek, [car] je demeure parmi les tentes de Qédar !
fr.B: Quel malheur pour moi de vivre en étranger à Méshek, d’habiter parmi les tentes de Qédar !
fr.R: Comme c’est dur pour moi ! Je suis comme un étranger qui vit loin, à Méshek, ou parmi les tentes de Qédar.

sw.L: Ole wangu, kwa kuwa ninakaa kama mgeni [katika] Mesheki, [kwamba] ninaishi kati ya mahema ya Kedari!
sw.B: Ni taabu kwangu, kuishi kama mgeni huko Mesheki, kufanya makao yangu kati ya mahema ya Kedari!
sw.R: Ni vibaya mno kwangu! Mimi ni kama mgeni anayeishi mbali huko Mesheki, au kati ya mahema ya Kedari.

decisions.choice: Meshech and Kedar: distant, warlike peoples
decisions.reason: Meshech was a people of the far north, in what is now Turkey (Genesis 10:2; Ezekiel 38:2); Kedar was a tribe of the Arabian desert, known for its archers (Genesis 25:13; Isaiah 21:16-17). The two lie far apart, so the psalmist is probably not living in both: the names are a picture of living among fierce, hostile people.

decisions.choice: sojourn: live as a foreigner
decisions.reason: The verb (gur) means to live somewhere as an outsider without the rights of a citizen.

decisions.choice: I am like a stranger
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the place names are a picture (m1).

decisions.choice: "Méshek" and "Qédar"
decisions.reason: The names are transcribed from the Hebrew with French spelling; Qédar keeps the q of the Hebrew as many French Bibles do. Both are distant peoples, as the meaning decision explains.

source.text: רַ֭בַּת שָֽׁכְנָה־לָּ֣הּ נַפְשִׁ֑י עִ֝֗ם שׂוֹנֵ֥א שָׁלֽוֹם׃

records.literal_gloss: Much has dwelt for itself my soul with [one who] hates peace.

en.L: Long has my soul dwelt with [one who] hates peace.
en.B: For far too long I have had to live beside people who hate peace.
en.R: I have spent too much of my life near people who hate peace.

fr.L: Longtemps mon âme a demeuré pour elle-même avec [celui qui] hait la paix.
fr.B: Depuis bien trop longtemps je dois vivre à côté de gens qui haïssent la paix.
fr.R: J’ai passé trop de temps de ma vie près de gens qui détestent la paix.

sw.L: Muda mrefu nafsi yangu imekaa pamoja na achukiaye amani.
sw.B: Kwa muda mrefu mno nimelazimika kuishi karibu na watu wanaochukia amani.
sw.R: Nimeishi muda mrefu sana karibu na watu wanaochukia amani.

decisions.choice: much: too long
decisions.reason: The word (rabbat) means "much" or "for a long time"; here it carries the sense of "far too long". It returns in 123:4 and 129:1-2.

decisions.choice: one who hates peace: a type
decisions.reason: The singular "one who hates" stands for the kind of people around the psalmist; verse 7 calls them "they".

decisions.choice: my soul (L); I (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in Psalms 1-12, nefesh is "soul" at Literal; Balanced and Readable say "me" or "my life", since the word means the whole living person.

decisions.choice: people who hate peace
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the singular type plural (m2), as verse 7 does.

records.literal_gloss: I [am] peace, and when I speak, they [are] for war.

en.L: I [am] peace; but when I speak, they [are] for war.
en.B: I stand for peace, but when I open my mouth, they choose war.
en.R: I want peace. But every time I speak, they want to fight.

fr.L: Moi, [je suis] paix ; mais quand je parle, eux [sont] pour la guerre.
fr.B: Moi, je suis pour la paix, mais dès que j’ouvre la bouche, ils choisissent la guerre.
fr.R: Moi, je veux la paix. Mais chaque fois que je parle, ils veulent se battre.

sw.L: Mimi [ni] amani; lakini ninaposema, wao [ni] kwa ajili ya vita.
sw.B: Mimi ninasimama upande wa amani, lakini ninapofungua kinywa changu, wao wanachagua vita.
sw.R: Mimi ninataka amani. Lakini kila ninaposema, wao wanataka kupigana.

decisions.choice: I am peace: I am wholly for peace
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says simply "I peace": the psalmist's whole self is set on peace, as the enemies are wholly "for war" (109:4 has "I prayer" in the same way).

decisions.choice: peace: whole and good relations
decisions.reason: Peace (shalom) is more than the absence of fighting: it is well-being and right relations between people. The word ties this psalm to the next (122:6-8).
